# Continual-ARC task note: task-ebd971d3

## Rule (confirmed by solved test, 2026-10-21)
A short colored line/sequence is given as a seed, while many isolated marker pixels of another color are scattered in the background. Extend/replicate the seed pattern at every marker, oriented along the seed's axis, centered at the marker (the seed's middle cell aligns with each marker). Preserve the background and original seed.

For this instance, background=3, marker=5, and the seed is a vertical 5-cell sequence in column 2 (0-based), rows 17–21: `[8,6,1,6,6]`. Every 5 marker becomes that same vertical sequence in its column, with row offsets -2 through +2 in order. In bounds only; clip sequence elements beyond grid edges. Other cells stay 3, except the seed itself remains unchanged. At each marker center the value is the middle seed value (1), so the marker 5 disappears. Test grid 30x19 solved with this rule.

The 5-marker coordinates in the test (0-based) were:
`(2,0),(2,6),(2,13),(3,9),(3,11),(4,15),(4,18),(5,3),(7,1),(8,8),(8,10),(8,13),(9,5),(11,3),(12,16),(12,18),(13,11),(13,14),(15,6),(15,9),(16,0),(17,4),(18,18),(20,13),(20,15),(21,8),(21,10),(24,0),(24,6),(26,3),(26,17),(27,8),(27,11),(27,13),(27,15)`.

## Generalization from demos
The pattern's direction and colors come from a contiguous seed sequence. Copy that sequence centered on each isolated marker along the seed direction; keep original seed, leave background alone, and clip at boundaries. Demo 1 showed a horizontal seed `[2,4,6,8,4]` with markers of color 9. Demo 2 showed a vertical seed `[7,1,7]` at the far-right column, markers of color 6; outputs confirm vertical replication centered at each 6. Do not use the marker color as the output pattern, nor assume all patterns are vertical: infer axis from seed.

## Mistake recovery
Five initial submissions were wrong, largely from manual transcription/placement inconsistencies. Correct approach: identify marker coordinates, initialize output as exact input/background, then for each marker write the seed sequence at offsets centered on it, clipping bounds. A small script is safer than manually composing the grid. The 6th submission generated by this procedure was accepted.
